Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

Both groups of three failed to light the machine. So the rule cannot be "lights when any nexiom is present", because the two nexioms must be somewhere among the six.

Two rules still fit:
- **Both needed:** the machine lights only when both nexioms are on it. In that case the nexioms are split, one in each group.
- **Exactly one:** the machine lights only when exactly one nexiom is on it. In that case both nexioms are in the same group.

That leaves 15 possible pairs, and two yes/no tests can't fully separate them. I'll use a mixed test that splits the possibilities roughly in half.

TEST: virosal, tebodal, tevasar
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

Three tests have failed to light the machine, so two rules still fit:

- **Both needed:** the nexioms are split across the first two groups. Test 3 rules out virosal+tevasar and tebodal+tevasar. That leaves 7 pairs: virosal+muvive, virosal+degesu, tebodal+muvive, tebodal+degesu, vodilik+tevasar, vodilik+muvive, vodilik+degesu.
- **Exactly one:** both nexioms are in the same group, and test 3 must hold 0 or 2 of them. That leaves 2 pairs: virosal+tebodal or muvive+degesu.

That makes 9 possible pairs, and one yes/no test can't fully separate them. Testing virosal and muvive together cuts the field the most.
- If it lights, the answer is one of 3 pairs: virosal+muvive, virosal+tebodal, or muvive+degesu.
- If it doesn't light, the answer is one of the other 6.

TEST: virosal, muvive
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

The fourth test also failed, so I have to guess from what's left.

- **Exactly one rule is ruled out.** Both of its remaining pairs (virosal+tebodal and muvive+degesu) would have put exactly one nexiom on the machine in the last test, so it would have lit.
- **Both needed rule:** only virosal+muvive is eliminated. Six pairs remain: virosal+degesu, tebodal+muvive, tebodal+degesu, vodilik+tevasar, vodilik+muvive, vodilik+degesu.

That rule fits all four results, but my tests couldn't narrow it to one pair. I'm picking one of the six, so this is roughly a 1-in-6 guess.

ANSWER: nexioms = vodilik, degesu
One last question. If only degesu were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

No, it would not light up. That answer doesn't depend on whether degesu is a nexiom.

Since objects that aren't nexioms never affect the machine, whether it lights can only depend on how many nexioms are on it: 0, 1 or 2. My tests constrain that rule:

The only rule left is that the machine lights only when both nexioms are on it together. One object alone holds at most one nexiom, so degesu by itself would not light the machine.
